description:
transport_test.rs's production_activation_order_has_one_typed_nontextual_authority scans a list of source files it calls production_order_owners, and that list includes include_str!("fixture_facts.rs").

fixture_facts is #[cfg(test)]-gated -- it is test-only support, not production. Auditing it as a production ordering authority is a category error: it makes the test assert something about code that never ships, and it will mislead the next reader about what fixture_facts is.

Remove that entry. Verify the remaining owners are all genuinely production modules while there.

Done when: production_order_owners lists only non-gated modules, and the full gate is green.

comments.text:
Premise was wrong: fixture_facts is ALREADY #[cfg(test)]-gated on main (compiler2/mod.rs declares it under #[cfg(test)]). My original scan looked for `pub fn` per file without checking whether the declaring module is gated, so canonical_call_edge_facts and render_canonical_call_edge_snapshot were false positives.

Same false-positive class hit the telemetry cluster: src/telemetry/capture.rs and src/telemetry/public_trace.rs are also already gated modules, which is why events, events_named, count_by_kind and spans_named appeared in the list.

Re-scoped to the one real residue below.

title: Stop auditing a test-only module as production order authority
